turns.text: Lloyd, I'm stuck on this Python error. 'Segmentation fault (core dumped)' when I run the eval script. Any ideas?
That usually points to a memory access violation in C extensions. Did you recently update numpy or torch? Also, check if you're accessing an out-of-bounds index in your custom loops.
I updated torch last night. I'll downgrade it. Btw, did you pick up the package I mentioned? The one with the GPU fans.
I don't have physical capabilities to pick up packages, Alan. Did you mean you want me to track a delivery? Or perhaps you ordered them yourself?

Right, forgot you're digital. I ordered them myself. It's for the new test rig. Anyway, I've been reading up on GWM-Robotics. Basically, it's an offline proxy for robot policy evaluation using general world models.
That sounds like a solid approach for reducing real-world wear and tear during training. Using world models as proxies can significantly speed up the iteration cycle.
Exactly. It's way cheaper than crashing real robots. I'm trying to replicate their setup. Do you know if their code is open source?
I'd need to check the latest repositories for you. Would you like me to search for the GWM-Robotics GitHub link?
Not yet. I'm just debugging this segfault first. If the torch downgrade fixes it, I'll send you the repo URL.
Understood. Let me know if the downgrade resolves the core dump.
